title: Reading age, period and cohort patterns
text: effect shape easy tell apart others: Age: rates peak age 45. Period: rates rise steeply 2010, epidemic. Cohort: people born 1955 1965 twice risk cohorts. pattern shown Lexis diagram (left) hexamap (right), 1960 birth cohort highlighted. figure uses color scale.
code: ages <- 15:70 periods <- 1999:2018  age <- function(a) -((a - 45) / 15)^2 period <- function(p) 0.12 * pmax(p - 2010, 0) cohort <- function(c) ifelse(c >= 1955 & c <= 1965, log(2), 0) compare <- function(rates, title) {   op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 1.5, 0))   on.exit(par(op))   lexis_map(rates, legend = FALSE, highlight = list(cohort = 1960, col = "white"))   hexamap(rates, highlight = list(cohort = 1960, col = "white"))   mtext(title, outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.2) }

title: Reading age, period and cohort patterns
text: Age effects follow age isolines: hexamap slope right (−30°); Lexis diagram horizontal. Period effects follow period isolines, vertical . Cohort effects follow cohort isolines: hexamap slope right (+30°); Lexis diagram diagonal (45°). hexamap three directions equally spaced, cohort band easy follow age period band.

title: Reading age, period and cohort patterns
text: cohort = period − age, linear trends age, period cohort separated: APC identification problem. example, linear increase age period gives exactly rates steeper linear increase age plus linear increase cohort: display can tell apart. hexamap shows departures linearity, peak, surge high-risk cohorts , without distorting three directions. Estimating separate effects needs APC model identifying assumption.
code: ap <- simulate_apc(ages, periods,                    age_effect = function(a) 0.02 * a,                    period_effect = function(p) 0.02 * p) ac <- simulate_apc(ages, periods,                    age_effect = function(a) 0.04 * a,                    cohort_effect = function(c) 0.02 * c) all.equal(ap, ac) #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with hexamap
text: traditional Lexis diagram, periods run along x axis ages along y axis, cohorts (birth years, period - age) run along diagonal. Relative age period, square grid compresses distance adjacent cohorts 30% (1−2/21 - \sqrt{2}/2), stretches distance cells cohort 41% (2−1\sqrt{2} - 1), makes adjacent cells cohort touch corner. hexagonal grid, three APC axes equal 60° angles neighboring cells share full edge along . grey tiles show one cell isolines grid.  tile centered x=32p,y=−p2,x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} p, \qquad y = - \frac{p}{2}, age aa period pp, neighboring tiles one age period group apart along every axis. apc_to_xy() returns coordinates.
code: mesh <- matrix(1, nrow = 5, ncol = 5, dimnames = list(1:5, 1:5)) mesh[3, 3] <- 2 par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) lexis_map(mesh, color_map = c("grey94", "grey60"), hex_border = "white",           hex_border_width = 2, isoline_interval = 1, legend = FALSE,           line_color = "grey30", title_text = "Square tiles") hexamap(mesh, color_map = c("grey94", "grey60"), hex_border = "white",         hex_border_width = 2, isoline_interval = 1, legend = FALSE,         line_color = "grey30", title_text = "Hexagonal tiles")

title: Getting started with hexamap
text: isoline_interval, first_age_isoline first_period_isoline set isolines drawn; cohort isolines pass crossings age period isolines. isolines chooses isolines draw. labels changes label prefixes. highlight draws chosen ages, periods cohorts highlighted lines.  default, cohort labels wrap around bottom hexamap. wrap_cohort_labels = FALSE, cohort isolines start left edge.

title: Getting started with hexamap
text: palette takes "jet" (default, paper) palette grDevices::hcl.pals(), perceptually uniform "viridis"; color_map takes vector colors. colorbar_range fixes limits; values outside get end colors. colorbar_scale maps values colors "linear", "log" "quantile" scale. quantile scale color covers share cells, brings patterns skewed data; colorbar shows percentiles left.  ratios differences, midpoint gives diverging scale centered value, limits symmetric around . , age’s rate divided rate 2010:
code: par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) hexamap(overdose_white_men, palette = "viridis", colorbar_scale = "log",         title_text = "viridis, log scale") hexamap(overdose_white_men, colorbar_scale = "quantile",         title_text = "jet, quantile scale") ratio <- overdose_white_men / overdose_white_men[, "2010"] hexamap(ratio, colorbar_scale = "log", midpoint = 1,         scale_units = "Rate ratio\nvs 2010")

title: Getting started with hexamap
text: hexamap() returns, invisibly, layout drew. hexamap_layout() computes object without drawing . layout holds one row per cell, age, period, cohort, value, coordinates color, along isolines color scale: Draw layout plot(), add annotations age period apc_to_xy():
code: lay <- hexamap_layout(overdose_white_men, colorbar_range = c(0, 40)) lay #> <hexamap_layout> (hexagon tiles) #>   Ages:    15-70  Periods: 1999-2018  Cohorts: 1929-2003 #>   Interval: 1 #>   Cells:   1120 (1100 drawn, 20 missing) #>   Scale:   linear, 0 to 40, 100 colors head(lay$cells) #>   age period cohort    value        x      y   color   fraction #> 1  15   1999   1984       NA 1731.185 -984.5    <NA>         NA #> 2  16   1999   1983       NA 1731.185 -983.5    <NA>         NA #> 3  17   1999   1982 1.694595 1731.185 -982.5 #00002E 0.04236488 #> 4  18   1999   1981 3.078342 1731.185 -981.5 #000050 0.07695855 #> 5  19   1999   1980 3.073404 1731.185 -980.5 #000050 0.07683509 #> 6  20   1999   1979 4.704179 1731.185 -979.5 #00007F 0.11760448 plot(lay, scale_units = "Deaths per 100,000") peak <- lay$cells[which.max(lay$cells$value), ] points(apc_to_xy(peak$age, peak$period), pch = 21, bg = "white", cex = 1.5) peak[, c("age", "period", "cohort", "value")] #>      age period cohort    value #> 1030  36   2017   1981 65.39119

title: Simulate age-period-cohort rates — simulate_apc
code: ages <- 15:70 periods <- 1999:2018 # a peak at age 45, a surge after 2010, and a high-risk 1955-1965 cohort rates <- simulate_apc(ages, periods,                       age_effect = function(a) -((a - 45) / 15)^2,                       period_effect = function(p) 0.15 * pmax(p - 2010, 0),                       cohort_effect = function(c) ifelse(c >= 1955 & c <= 1965, 0.7, 0)) hexamap(rates, scale_units = "Rate per 100,000")   # with Poisson noise for 100,000 persons per cell set.seed(1) noisy <- simulate_apc(ages, periods, age_effect = function(a) -((a - 45) / 15)^2,                       population = 1e5) head(attr(noisy, "counts")[, 1:5]) #>    1999 2000 2001 2002 2003 #> 15    0    0    0    1    1 #> 16    0    0    0    0    0 #> 17    0    0    0    0    0 #> 18    1    1    0    1    0 #> 19    0    0    1    1    1 #> 20    2    0    3    1    0

title: hexamap 0.1.2
text: colorbar longer draws shifted, overlapping color blocks (2:ncol+1 evaluated 3:(ncol+1)). Every palette color can now appear hexagons. Previously top color never used ncol breaks gave ncol - 1 bins. NA cells skipped instead making default color range fail “‘’ must finite number”. Data finite values give clear error. log color scale longer fails zeros: values <= 0 drawn lowest color, warning. non-positive colorbar_range log scale gives error. colorbar_scale accepts "linear", "log" "quantile" (legacy names "Normal", "Log", "Percentile") letter case. Unknown names give clear error instead “object ‘data_cutpoints’ found”. Colorbar tick labels correct palettes length (assumed 100 colors). now show 3 significant digits, small rates longer rounded 0. Percentile ticks drawn quantile scale. hexamap() restores graphical parameters changes. empty subtitle_text longer drawn “NA”. scale_units now displayed colorbar, documented. Inputs validated informative errors. Data frames numeric columns accepted.
